verdict.reasoning: Patient reports feeling unwell for “a good few days” and specifies onset on Saturday, about “five days ago,” with cough, cold (runny nose), and sore throat and feeling run-down: “I just feel a bit, run-down, you know I've got, a cough, a cold… it would have been that Saturday… about five days ago.”

Patient describes cough as “mostly dry” with some in the morning: “mostly, dry… in the morning it's a bit worse,” and then acknowledges some phlegm: “So you're not bringing up any mucky, flem?” / “Yeah… It's a wee bit….” This supports mostly dry cough with some sputum, especially in the morning.

Shortness of breath without chest pain: “So you're… feeling more short of breath?” / “Yeah, yeah.” and “any pain in your chest at all?” / “No, no… it's just a wee bit shortness of breath… it's not pain.” Night fevers/chills: “have you noticed… temperatures or fevers?… feeling hot and cold? Sweaty?” / “Yeah, yeah that's… definitely something I've noticed. Like… in bed with the wife and having to… get out and, get the blanket off, and put it back on again.”

Myalgias: “any kind of muscle pain, joint pains?” / Patient: “Yeah… just a wee bit stiffer than normal… elbows and knees… all over.” Transient diarrhea day 1 now resolved: “the first day I had, you know a wee bit… of diarrhoea… but that, that's, that's fine, now.”
Appetite and fluids: “how's your appetite? Are you eating and drinking OK?” / “my appetite's been, been all right yeah, yeah. I'm trying to, trying to keep, keep the fluids up as well.”
Patient explicitly: “I've got the uh, I've got the diabetes.” Doctor: “Diabetes, right. What type… is it type one or type two?” Patient: “it's, it's uh, type, two, two.”

Patient reports prior high blood pressure: “when I was speaking to… another doctor… he took my blood pressure and that said that was… higher than it should be.” Doctor: “You've been diagnosed with high blood pressure… OK.” This supports hypertension as PMH.
Patient describes being overweight: “I'm a wee bit, on the chunky side… I've got a wee bit round the midriff, the spare tyre's definitely there.”
Medications: “it's… Metformin?” / Doctor: “that's correct.”
Medications: “and, and there's another one, Lisinopril? … that's those two.” Doctor: “Lisinopril, yeah.”
OTC aspirin: “just those two. Yeah, I mean a wee bit of like, a wee bit of Aspirin or whatever every now and again, but you know nothing long-term.”

No known drug allergies: “Do you have any allergies at all?” Patient: “not that I'm aware of… No, nothing, nothing that, nothing that I'm aware of, doctor's never said nothing to me.” Doctor clarifies it’s about medications.

Lives with wife: “you said you live, with your wife… Anyone else at home with you?” / “no, no, kids… flown the nest. So now it's just me and the missus.” Job: “there's a wee factory, just down the road… we just manufacture like… kind of steel, steel parts.”
Alcohol intake: “maybe what like four, four pints on like Saturday and then… Sunday as well… maybe like. Nine, nine pints in a week, I would say.”
Smoking and vaping: “a wee, every now and again, but I'm… trying to cut that down. I've got a wee… vaporisers… I've been cutting down on the cigarettes.”

Doctor’s assessment: “what you essentially have is a bit of a, a bit of a viral illness perhaps, a bit of a, maybe early signs of a flu… I don't think you've got a chest infection, but what we could think about is giving you a script for antibiotics… if… still feeling breathless.” This supports viral URTI/flu-like illness with concern about early LRT involvement (hence safety-net antibiotics).
While T2DM and metformin use are documented, there is no statement about diabetes control or stability: no sugars, control comments, or complications mentioned. “Stable” is not supported.
Hypertension and lisinopril use are recorded, but there is no assessment that blood pressure is controlled or “stable” on lisinopril in this transcript.

Tobacco: “a wee [smoke], every now and again… cutting down on the cigarettes… got… vaporiser.” Alcohol: “I do like a wee drink… maybe… nine pints in a week.” This supports use of both tobacco and alcohol.

Doctor advises: “what you essentially have is… a viral illness… things… you can do… stay rested, drink plenty of fluids… if you are feeling hot and cold and sweaty, taking regular Paracetamol would be beneficial.”

Antibiotics plan: “I'm a little bit on the edge about giving you antibiotics… what we could think about is giving you a script for antibiotics… give it about twenty four to forty eight hours. If you feel like you're still feeling breathless and, run-down, I think there's no harm in starting a course of antibiotics, something like Amoxicillin. One tablet, three times a day.”
Metformin use is confirmed, but there is no explicit instruction in the plan to “continue metformin”; diabetes medications are not discussed in the management part of the consultation.
Lisinopril use is confirmed, but the doctor does not explicitly address continuation or adjustment; hypertension meds are not mentioned in the plan.

Smoking and alcohol counseling: doctor says regarding vaping/quit attempt, “I wish you all the best on your journey to quit, I highly recommend it… it'll certainly help your health,” and earlier notes old doctor said he was drinking “a wee bit too much,” implying concern and moderation advice. This supports encouragement of smoking cessation and moderation of alcohol consumption.
Follow-up: “if you're still not better by next week, come back and see me, we can have another look.”
